newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-UNKNOWN BEAN BETWEEN MOORER AND A BIG PAYDAY.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-UNKNOWN BEAN BETWEEN MOORER AND A BIG PAYDAY.

text.p: Michael Moorer's International Boxing Federation heavyweight crown and his spot in line for a big money shot at Mike Tyson or Evander Holyfield will be at stake Saturday when he fights lightly regarded challenger Vaughn Bean.
"I just have to go out there and be focused on what I have to do," Moorer said in a tele-conference call last week for the fight at the Las Vegas Hilton.

"The motivation for me is to focus on Vaughn Bean because he is going to try to take away my title," said Moorer (38-1), who became champion for the second time in June by outpointing German Axel Schulz for the vacant IBF title.
"I can't talk about Tyson-Holyfield right now," Moorer said.
In stark contrast, Moorer's promoter, Dino Duva, was looking ahead to a possible title unification meeting with the winner of the May 3 Tyson-Holyfield rematch.
"Once he gets rid of Bean he is looking for bigger and better things," Duva said.
Holyfield holds the World Boxing Association (WBA) heavyweight belt after upsetting Tyson last November.

Also looking for bigger and better things later this year, is the former six-time champion Julio Cesar Chavez (98-2-1), who will fight American Tony Martin (34-5-1) in a junior welterweight non-title 10-rounder.
The 34-year-old Mexican will be fighting for the second time since being bloodied and beaten by Oscar De La Hoya in four rounds last June.
"What I have to do is take care of myself like I used to and in September I'll be champion of the world again," said Chavez.

First Chavez must re-focus his mind on Martin. Chavez was originally set to fight Martin, who dropped out and was replaced by Gary Kirkland. Only last week, Martin was put back on the card as Chavez's opponent.
"I am a little uncomfortable with the change of opponents," said Chavez, who won his last outing against Joey Gamache in October.
"I was preparing for one, now I am fighting another," said Chavez. "Tony Martin is a very strong fighter who throws a lot of punches."
While Chavez expects to face a lot of punches, few boxing insiders see Moorer having to struggle to beat the unknown Bean, who is rated only fifth by the IBF.
"It's big step up for him," Moorer's trainer Teddy Atlas said of Bean, whose 27-0 record has been complied against weak opposition. "It's like going from the wading pool to the ocean."
Moorer on the other hand has taken on some of the best in the business. He beat Holyfield to win the title in 1994, only to lose in the next fight to George Foreman by a one punch knockout.
"People who don't give him much of a chance know the type of fighter I am," said Moorer, a 7-to-1 betting favourite.
"I'm on a totally different level," Moorer said. "He has to step up to my level, which he has never done before, and I'm going to put him right back down to the level where he belongs."
Bean hopes to make the most of his big chance.
"This is my opportunity to show the world what I can do and I am going to do it," said Bean. "I am going to be heavyweight champion of the world."

In two other title bouts, World Boxing Council straweight champion Ricardo Lopez of Mexico (44-0) will defend against Mongkol Charoen of Thailand (20-1); and WBA junior middleweight champion Laurent Boudouani of France (34-2) will defend against American Carl Daniels (38-2).
